paper.title_en: Log-normal behavior of Optical Polarization in a sample of Blazars: Evidence for Multiplicative Magneto-hydrodynamic Processes in Relativistic Jets
paper.abstract_en: Optical synchrotron polarization is one of the most direct probes of the magnetic-field structure and particle-acceleration processes in the relativistic jets of blazars. Although long-term optical flux variability is often attributed to multiplicative stochastic processes because of its log-normal behavior, but the physical origin of optical polarization variability remains less understood. In this study, we investigate the long-term optical flux and polarization variability of a sample of blazars using nearly a decade of photo-polarimetric observations from the Steward Observatory. We find that, like the optical flux, the optical degree of polarization is generally well described by a log-normal distribution and shows an approximately linear relationship between its variability amplitude and mean value. We interpret this behavior within a magneto-hydrodynamic (MHD) framework in which the magnetic-field undergoes repeated stochastic changes driven by shocks, turbulence, velocity shear, and large-scale jet dynamics. The cumulative effect of these processes can naturally generate multiplicative variability, leaving similar statistical signatures in both the synchrotron flux and the degree of polarization. Our results provide new observational evidence that the long-term statistical behavior of optical flux and polarization may arise from a common set of MHD processes associated with magnetic-field evolution.
